The bug in [`NumberUtils.createNumber`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_1_group_d_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/math/NumberUtils.java#L466-L476) was caused by determining the target numeric type based solely on raw hex digit count (`str.length() - pfxLen`). This failed in two ways:
1. Leading zeros artificially increased the digit count, causing values fitting within `Integer` or `Long` to be parsed into wider numeric types (`Long` or `BigInteger`).
2. For 8-digit and 16-digit positive hex numbers, when the first significant digit is greater than `'7'` (i.e. `8..F`), the values exceed `Integer.MAX_VALUE` (`0x7FFFFFFF`) and `Long.MAX_VALUE` (`0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`), causing `Integer.decode()` or `Long.decode()` to throw `NumberFormatException`.

### Changes Made:
- In [`NumberUtils.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_1_group_d_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/math/NumberUtils.java#L466-L477), stripped leading zeros and checked the first significant digit (`firstSigDigit > '7'`) to properly choose between `Integer`, `Long`, and `BigInteger`.
- Generated the focused patch file [enlightened_fix.patch](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_1_group_d_fix/enlightened_fix.patch).
